principle: Core Composite Components are stable, directly reusable assemblies built from Core Components. They have a concrete anatomy and interaction contract, but they must not encode product-domain names, routes, state enums or business copy.

composites.name: Carousel
composites.intent: Present a small ordered set of peer content panels that users can move through without losing orientation or accessibility.
rules: Manual swipe or scroll-snap MUST work without autoplay or pointer-only controls.
Autoplay MUST be off by default. When enabled it SHOULD use an interval of at least 5 seconds, pause after user interaction or focus, and stop or collapse under reduced-motion preferences.
If motion continues beyond 5 seconds, users MUST have a way to pause or stop it.
Visible indicators MAY be visually small, but their interactive hit areas MUST meet platform touch-target guidance.
Previous/next controls MUST NOT obscure meaningful slide content; mobile layouts MAY omit overlay arrows when swipe and indicators are sufficient.
Slide changes SHOULD be announced for user-initiated navigation without producing repeated screen-reader announcements for passive autoplay.
A slide SHOULD have one clear primary destination; avoid nested full-card links plus overlapping child actions.
avoid: autoplay as the only way to reveal content
tiny indicator dots as tiny tap targets
overlay arrows covering titles or actions
different slide heights causing the page to jump

composites.name: Filter Bar
composites.intent: Provide a reusable mobile collection control that combines optional query input, filter entry, active-condition summary and result feedback while keeping committed state authoritative outside the composite.
rules: Pending query input and committed query MAY be separate states; submission behavior MUST be explicit and predictable.
The parent collection MUST remain the authoritative owner of committed query and filter values.
Opening the filter surface SHOULD initialize a local draft from committed state; dismissing without Apply MUST NOT mutate committed state.
The filter trigger SHOULD show an active count or equivalent state cue without becoming a page-level Primary action.
Inside the draft surface, Apply MAY be the single Primary action for that action group; Reset SHOULD be Tertiary or text treatment and MUST reset the draft before commitment.
Applied conditions SHOULD be individually removable when space and scanability benefit from it.
After commitment, result count or a meaningful result update SHOULD be exposed through an accessible status region.
Returning from a detail view SHOULD preserve committed filter state while the collection task is still active.
avoid: committing every option tap when users are comparing several conditions
keeping a second authoritative filter truth inside the sheet after Apply
brand-filling the trigger, chips and sheet footer at the same time
using disabled Apply as the only indication that nothing changed

composites.name: Tabbed Action Bar
composites.intent: Combine peer-view navigation with a small, stable set of local utility actions without compressing tabs or turning a navigation row into an icon toolbar.
rules: Tabs remain the primary structure; utility actions MUST NOT reduce tab hit targets below platform guidance.
On narrow mobile widths, keep at most two local utility actions inline; move additional actions to overflow or a more appropriate Top App Bar before shrinking labels or hit areas.
Global actions such as account-wide notifications SHOULD live in the Top App Bar rather than being repeated inside every tabbed local navigation row.
Active tab state MUST use readable text plus the normal Tabs indicator; do not convert the whole row into multiple brand-filled pills.
Tab labels MUST remain single-line. Use scrollable Tabs before truncating several peer labels into ambiguous abbreviations.
Selecting a tab SHOULD update selection immediately; asynchronous content loading belongs below the bar and MUST NOT make the selected tab appear uncertain.
Web implementations SHOULD support tablist keyboard behavior; mobile implementations MUST preserve full-row touch targets and predictable focus order.
avoid: three or more equally weighted icon actions squeezing three tabs on a narrow screen
putting global notification, local filter and local search into the same cramped row by default
brand-filled pill tabs mixed with brand-filled utility buttons
reordering tabs when an action badge appears

composites.name: Grouped List
composites.intent: Present several related destinations, settings or attributes as one calm stacked group so users scan relationships without a card-per-row layout.
rules: Use one shared group surface for related rows instead of wrapping every row in its own Card.
Rows SHOULD use a minimum visual height around 52-56 logical units while preserving platform touch-target minimums.
The whole row SHOULD be the activation target when the row navigates; a chevron then indicates destination rather than acting as a separate tiny button.
Switch rows MUST NOT also expose a navigation chevron unless there are clearly separated actions with distinct labels and hit regions.
Dividers SHOULD be subtle and MAY begin at the content column rather than cutting through the leading visual area.
Leading icon containers SHOULD default to neutral subtle treatment; use Brand tint only when selection, identity or meaning requires it, not on every row for decoration.
Pressed and focus states SHOULD apply to the row surface, not only to the trailing accessory.
Destructive actions SHOULD be separated or placed at the end with Danger text; avoid a permanently red group surface.
avoid: card inside card for every setting row
purple icon tile on every row regardless of meaning
chevron plus switch producing two unclear actions
divider lines darker than the content hierarchy
